## 4. Engine design
### 4.1 Mod project model + revisions (size L)
Typed project: `ModSpec`/content IR (items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, biomes...), code files, assets, datapacks, config, dependencies, tests, requirement IDs. Stored as immutable revisions with diffs; each revision traces to exact inputs and toolchain; the last passing revision is always preserved. `schemaVersion` with explicit migrations; JSON Schema as the portable contract, Zod types in code. New tables (project, revision, asset, namespace) need an owner-approved DB migration deploy. Chat history is not the project.

### 4.2 Registries and reserved namespaces (S-M)
Capability registry, **version registry**, **identifier registry**, asset registry with provenance. Each project reserves a namespace `nx_<hash>` at creation so IDs, keys, permissions, sound keys, glyph ranges and model paths are collision-free by construction. Version registry holds exact pack format per version (one `pack.mcmeta` style per version family), JDK, classpath hash, capability flags (item model definitions from 1.21.4; Dialog API 1.21.7+; Folia support), status (`preview/supported/deprecated/blocked`). Contract-tested against Paper's Fill API.

### 4.3 Capability router + task spec (M)
After the prompt check: classify what the request needs (plugin / plugin + resource pack / datapack / future client mod), disclose limits, show an editable plan and acceptance criteria before tokens are spent. One schema: this is the Master Plan's `CyrusTaskSpec`, the Roadmap's Mod Specification and the asset manifest. Tier gate is applied here and again inside the build service request.

### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
Deterministic generators emit code/data/packs for common mechanics from the IR; free-form AI code is the fallback. Build: `javac` per version lane (JDK 21 and JDK 25 side by side, per-version `--release`, classpath files fetched by checksum, exact stable pin), scan, package. Make jars byte-stable (`jar --date`, sorted inputs); record **engine release id** (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report and SBOM per artifact. Rename CYR-004 to "immutable javac/classpath/template".

### 4.5 Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting (M)
- **ManagedPlugin** records: pinned version per Minecraft family, installed on first dependent mod, ref-counted, not user-removable while depended on. Hosts the Pack Loader and BetterModel.
- **Nxeon Pack Loader**: sends N packs by UUID with `addResourcePack`, per-pack required/optional, accept-rate telemetry, Geyser/Floodgate detection. `server.properties` only as fallback. Conflict engine detects an existing pack owner (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo).
- **Pack hosting**: object storage on an Nxeon domain (provider not named to customers), content-addressed immutable URLs `/p/<sha1>.zip`, size caps, retention GC; keep it off the primary node.

### 4.6 Test Flight (M, lite first)
Disposable Paper server per target version on node-2 (MEASURED 2026-10-10 with Test Flight lite: 26.x 10.4-10.8 s boot, 722-803 MB peak RSS; 1.21.11 on JDK 21 18.0 s, 878 MB; whole flight 12-20 s; see docs "Cyrus Test Flight (R0)"): boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown. Later: MockBukkit logic tests, Mineflayer scenario bots (MIT, supports through 26.1), performance scenarios. Honest per-check status table; no "success" if a required stage was skipped. Concurrency capped (a past node crash came from parallel builds).

### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
- **Studios**: v1 minimal (miniPaint MIT stopgap or a small pixel editor; wavesurfer.js BSD waveform with trim/fade/layer and JSON edit recipes), then the full editors in R3. Library browsing follows the studio gate.

### 4.8 Conflict engine and Mod Packs (L)
- **Server inventory** first: read-only scan of jars' descriptors, `server.properties`, datapacks, existing pack owners. This is the conflict engine's input (and the "Server Doctor" feature below).
- **Static classes**: plugin names, commands/aliases (incl. Brigadier root literals and vanilla overrides), permissions, depend/softdepend/loadbefore DAG, api-version/Java/Folia, registered events + priorities, NamespacedKey/PDC keys, legacy `custom_model_data` integers and `item_model` keys, recipe keys, sound event keys, single-owner resources (Vault economy/permission provider, chat renderer, tab list, sidebar, world rules), datapack `replace:true` tags and double-overridden vanilla ids, resource-pack whole-file overrides, `sounds.json`/atlas/lang merges, font codepoint overlap, unmergeable shaders, budget classes (display entities, tasks, pack size).
- **Resolution**: reserved namespaces prevent most clashes; command alias rewrites; priority ordering; Pack Loader stacking; evaluate Weld/Beet (MIT) as an offline merge subprocess behind golden tests. Severity report: blocking / warn / info.
- **Dynamic**: one combined boot and one differential boot per changed mod; pairwise only for statically flagged pairs.
- **Mod Pack**: an Nxeon manifest shaped like mrpack (files with path/sha1/sha512/downloads/env, override dirs, platform=paper). Third-party jars by URL + hash, only Cyrus-built artifacts embedded. Versioned, changelog, compatibility matrix, combined test report; installs and rolls back as one unit; never contains Paper/vanilla jars. Not gated by plan.

### 4.9 Import your own mod (L)
Source-only first: copy `src/main/java|resources`, drop and ignore the uploader's build files (their build is never run), compile with the service template and a **curated checksum-pinned dependency allowlist** (also the basis for first-class integrations: Vault, LuckPerms, PlaceholderAPI as soft bridge). Unsupported: Kotlin, Lombok, annotation processors. Ingestion limits (zip-slip, zip bomb ratio, nested jars, multi-release, class major), no execution at ingestion, ownership attestation record, detected licence, public sharing only with consent. Two scan profiles: strict for generated, **attested/imported** with warnings and no "safe" claim. Imported source becomes revision 0 and uses the same change planner, tests, versions and install path. Jar-only imports are analysis and diagnosis only (decompile for navigation, never into shared knowledge). Not gated by plan; model use and assets follow tokens and the asset gates.

### 4.10 Per-game adapter contract (S, define in R0)
Artifact types and routes; toolchain profile and deny-list scan; version registry; knowledge pack; asset formats and **delivery** (Minecraft: server-pushed pack; Valheim: client zip; Terraria/Palworld: none; tModLoader: client mod); install rules; test lane; maturity level. Add `game` to every id and registry. Texture/Sound studios light up only where the adapter declares an asset format and delivery path. A realistic 3D/PBR profile is a later track; build only the interfaces now.

### 4.11 Data packs (M)
Typed spec -> per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation then boot a real headless Paper and test over RCON. MVP: recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. Worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions) later; `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so those changes need a restart.

## 5. Roadmap (ordered by dependency)
Calendar note: the review estimated R0-R2 at about 5-7 weeks including owner waits (UNVERIFIED judgement). The owner has beaten estimates; treat these as sequencing and relative size, not promises. (T) = real Minecraft client needed, (O) = owner action.

### R0 Foundation (about 4 working days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |

| 1 | Launch gates (verify hardened scan live (O), per-build engine-release record, paired flag guard, free-build abuse limit, per-build cost cap). ### Cyrus engine core (R0)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r0` (2026-10-10). Plan: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/MASTER-PLAN.md` sections 4.1-4.3, 4.10 and R0; code audit `G-gaps.md`. **Nothing here is wired into the build pipeline yet** (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts` is unchanged): builds still run exactly as before, and the new tables stay empty until a later slice writes to them.

**Version-support registry** (`lib/cyrus/versions/registry.{ts,json}`, R0 day 1). One row per Minecraft version: family, `javaRelease` (21 for 1.21.x, 25 for 26.x), `status` (supported / preview / legacy / blocked), `buildable` (true only for what the build service compiles today: 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11), exact `paperCoordinate` (null for 26.x until a stable build is pinned), resource/data pack formats (null = unverified, consumers fail closed) and capability flags (`itemModelDefinitions` 1.21.4+, `dialogApi` 1.21.7+, `adventure5`). `resourcePackFormat()` replaces the old `packFormatFor` guesswork. The same JSON is readable by the plain-Node build service.

**Layout.** `lib/cyrus/engine-core/` is the game-agnostic core and must never name a game; `lib/cyrus/adapters/` holds the per-game facts.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `engine-core/spec.ts` | ModSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateModSpec` + `migrateSpec` + `modSpecJsonSchema()` |
| `engine-core/modspec.v1.schema.json` | the portable JSON Schema contract; regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus-modspec-schema.ts` (a test fails while it is stale) |
| `engine-core/identifiers.ts` | namespaces, identifier formats, glyph codepoints, `detectCollisions` (pure) |
| `engine-core/revisions.ts` | manifest validation, `diffManifests`, engine record (pure) |
| `engine-core/store.ts` | the only writer of the four tables (server only) |
| `engine-core/router.ts` | deterministic capability router |
| `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | plan-tier asset gate + router downgrade |
| `adapters/types.ts`, `adapters/minecraft.ts`, `adapters/index.ts` | `GameAdapter` contract, adapter #1, `getAdapter(game)` |

**ModSpec v1.** `schemaVersion` (1), `game` (adapter id), `target.version` (must be in the adapter's version registry; a preview version is valid but warns `version_not_buildable`; `blocked` is an error), `namespace` (the project's reserved `nx_<8>`), `summary`, `routes` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod), `requirements` with stable ids `REQ-1..` and priority must/should/could, `nonGoals`, `constraints`, `assets` slots `{ id, kind: texture|sound|model|ui, purpose, source, requirementIds }`, `tests` (acceptance plan `T-1..`: compile / scan / boot / functional / manual, `covers` REQ ids), `install` (side, restartRequired, clientSteps, notes). Unknown keys are rejected. Validation never throws: it returns `{ ok, spec | errors, warnings }`, each issue `{ path, code, message }` (codes include `missing_schema_version`, `schema_too_new`, `no_migration`, `unknown_game`, `unknown_version`, `duplicate_id`, `unknown_requirement`; warnings `untested_requirement`, `route_unsupported`, `asset_kind_undeliverable`). Migrations: `SPEC_MIGRATIONS[n]` rewrites version n to n+1; empty while v1 is the only version. Asset `source`: `generate`, `library`, `upload`, `edit` bring new or changed content (gated); `existing`, `imported` keep what the project holds (never gated).

**Projects and revisions** (`store.ts`). `createProject({ userId, game, title?, rootBuildId? })` reserves a unique namespace (`namespaceFromSeed(projectId)`, retried with a new seed on a clash; `rootBuildId` optionally links a ModBuild chain, unique). `addRevision(projectId, { kind: generated|edited|imported|asset, manifest, spec?, modBuildId?, engine?, status?, message?, expectedHeadId? })` validates the spec (and that its game/namespace are the project's), the manifest (`[{ path, sha256, role }]`, safe relative paths, unique, stored sorted) and the engine record (prompt version, sheets with hashes, rules version, scanner hash, image digest, model, toolchain: only what is known), then appends under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the project row: gap-free `seq`, `parentId` = previous head, head moves; `expectedHeadId` gives an optimistic `stale_head` refusal. `setRevisionStatus` is the one allowed change: pending -> passed | failed, once; a pass becomes `lastPassingRevisionId` only if it is newer than the current one, so a later failure never loses the last good revision. `getHead`, `lastPassing`, `listRevisions`, `diffRevisions` (added / removed / changed files), `revertTo(projectId, targetId)` = a NEW `revert` revision copying the target's spec, manifest, build link and status (`revertOfId`, `engine.revertOf`); history is kept. `recordAsset` stores content-addressed assets (same content twice = one row). Errors are `EngineStoreError` with a `code`.

**Immutability in the database.** Section 2 of the manual migration adds a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger on `CyrusRevision`: any change to content columns raises, and `status` may only go pending -> passed | failed. `prisma db push` does not create triggers, so it is applied by hand with the migration (the DB test applies the same SQL to its throwaway DB). Deletes stay allowed (account/project deletion).

**Namespaces and identifiers.** Kinds `item`, `model` (path with `/`), `sound` (dotted), `permission` and `config` (`nx_x.a.b`), `command`, `recipe`, `glyph`; `buildIdentifier(ns, kind, key)`, `parseIdentifier`, `validateIdentifier(kind, id, ownNamespace)`. `CyrusIdentifier` is unique per (namespace, kind, key); `reserveIdentifier` is idempotent. Glyphs: each namespace has a home block of 256 codepoints in the supplementary Private Use Areas (U+F0000 and U+100000 planes, 510 blocks; the crowded BMP PUA is not used); a full block moves on to the next. `codepoint` is unique across ALL projects, so Mod Packs cannot collide on glyphs. `detectCollisions(records)` (pure) reports duplicate ids (case-insensitive), duplicate codepoints and invalid ids across any set: a project, a pack, a server.

**GameAdapter** (`adapters/types.ts`, MASTER-PLAN 4.10): artifact types per route with availability `available | planned | unsupported`, default route, toolchain profile (compiler, release per version, scanner path), knowledge source, version list with capabilities, asset delivery per kind, install rules, test lane, maturity (`planned | template | beta | stable`) and the router's `routeRules`. **Minecraft** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`) reads the version registry and `lib/cyrus/games/minecraft.ts` and changes neither; maturity `beta`; only `plugin` is available today; `resourcePack` and `dataPack` are `planned`; `clientMod` is `unsupported`; all four asset kinds deliver via a server-pushed resource pack (planned); boot/functional tests `planned`.

**Capability router** (`router.ts`, no AI call). `routeSpec(spec, adapter, { prompt?, gate?: { plan } })` matches the adapter's rules against summary + requirements + asset purposes + prompt (never non-goals or constraints) and asset kinds, and returns `routes`, split into `available / planned / unsupported`, a `label` (`plugin`, `plugin+resourcePack`, `dataPack`, ... or `clientMod-unsupported`), `buildableNow`, `limits` (`info | warn | block` with plain-English text) and the matched rule ids. Minecraft limits: custom blocks, free-form HUD widgets, keybinds and custom sky need a client mod; native entity models need a client mod (skinned vanilla mobs / display entities instead); Dialog API needs 1.21.7+; item models need 1.21.4+; worldgen needs a restart; a preview or unknown target version blocks; planned routes say "not built yet". With `gate`, the asset gate runs first and strips gated assets (warn limits `asset_gate:<id>`), and a gated asset named only in words adds a `<rule>:plan` notice instead of a route.

**Plan-tier asset gate** (`asset-gate.ts`, owner decisions). `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`: `create` and `edit` (also automatic generation inside a build, library picks and uploads) need `saka` for sound and `all` for texture; `model` and `ui` follow texture (top plan). `keep`, `install`, `export`, `rebuild`, `import` (your own mod) and `compose` (Mod Packs) are never gated, for any plan or none. Unknown plan / token state -> `plan_unknown` denial for create/edit only (fail closed). `normalizePlan` is the one mapping of plan names (`all` = `yakko` = "All models"; free, katara, saka). `gateSpecAssets` lists denials (the build service request must run it again), `downgradeSpecAssets` strips gated slots with a customer-visible reason and leaves requirements in place. Wiring into `gateBuild`/`create.ts` is left for the asset slice (R1): builds carry no spec or assets yet, so there is nothing to gate there today.

**Tests.** `test/cyrus-engine-core.test.ts` (pure: spec, migrations, JSON Schema file, identifiers, collisions, manifests, adapter, router, the 40-case gate matrix and more). `test/cyrus-engine-store-db.test.ts` (opt-in, throwaway DB only): `devhost db push`, then `devhost run --lock -- env CYRUS_ENGINE_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-engine-store-db.test.ts`.

**Deploy (owner).** Review and apply `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql` (four new tables + the trigger; no ALTER/DROP of anything existing). Nothing in the app reads the tables yet, so the migration can land before or with the code.

## Cyrus R0 guards (2026-10-10)

- **Version registry** (`lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json` + `registry.ts`): one row per Minecraft version (Java release, resource/data pack formats, capabilities, `buildable`, `status`). Pack formats fail closed: unknown versions and the unverified 26.2 number throw; 26.x packs need an explicit `allowPreview`; 1.21.1 is refused for item-model packs; built packs report `packClientVerified` (false until a real client has loaded one). `buildable` versions must equal `MB_VERSIONS` (tested).
- **Launch pair** (`lib/cyrus/launch-state.ts`): the studio flag (`cyrus_studio_public_enabled`) and the token economy (`cyrus_tok_live`) must both be on before the public can build. Studio public + tokens off is an invalid "unmetered" state: `studioPublicEffective()` returns false and `gateBuild` refuses non-preview accounts (`code: launch_pair`) instead of letting them build for free on any model. Private-preview accounts are unaffected.
- **Starter-grant abuse guard** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/starter-guard.ts`): one free build per real person. Alias addresses (dots, +tags, googlemail) share one grant (dedupe via the ledger idempotency key on a hash of the normalized email); throwaway-inbox domains get none (they can still buy tokens). The disposable list is a baseline: extend it from real abuse. Per-IP/device caps are not built yet (need request context + storage).
- **Per-build cost cap**: already enforced in the build service (`MB_BUILD_BUDGET_USD` default 4, `MB_CALL_BUDGET_USD` default 2.5, `server.js` ~57); not changed.
- **Reproducible jars** (`services/modbuilder/jar.js`): sorted entries + fixed `--date`, with a fallback to the old invocation if the JDK rejects it. Not verified against a real JDK yet: check one real build on VM 88001 after the next image rebuild (and that the same source gives the same sha256 twice).

## Cyrus Test Flight (R0)

"Test Flight lite" (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r0`, **not wired into the build path, nothing deployed**): boot ONE throwaway real Paper server for one registry version on node-2, load the given plugin jars / datapacks, run the checks, tear it down, return a JSON report. Master plan 4.6.

**Files**
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/runner.js`: the runner (plain Node, no deps; runs on node-2 as root). `node runner.js run <resolved-spec.json>` prints the report JSON; `node runner.js setup 21|25` fetches + verifies a pinned JDK.
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/lib.js`: its pure helpers (log matchers + default ignores, plugin.yml-from-jar reader, `plugins` reply parser, RCON wire format, server.properties, resolved-spec validation).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/fixtures/`: `hello` (positive control, `/tfhello`), `broken` (throws in onEnable), `datapack-tf_smoke` (one function), `build.sh` (javac `--release N -proc:none` against a classpath file + reproducible `jar --date`, same as the build service).
- `lib/cyrus/testflight/types.ts` (spec/report types), `spec.ts` (`validateSpec`, `resolveSpec`, `requiredStages`; fail closed on the registry), `summary.ts` (`summarize`, `mergeSummaries`, `describe`), `client.ts` (`runTestFlight`, `sshRemote`, injectable `Remote`).
- Tests: `test/cyrus-testflight.test.ts` (pure, 23 tests), `test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts` (real node-2 runs, run by hand: `tsx test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts all --out r.json`).
- Registry: `paperBuild`/`paperServerSha256` now also pin the **server** jar for 1.21.11 (build 132, Fill STABLE). A version without a server pin cannot be test-flown (1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 today).

**Checks, in order** (each `pass` / `fail` / `not_run` with evidence lines; a check never passes unless it ran):
1. `boot_done`: a `Done (Xs)!` line within `bootSec` (default 180).
2. `plugins_enabled`: per plugin (name read from the jar's plugin.yml / paper-plugin.yml): log has `Enabling <name> v`, no `Error occurred while enabling`, no `Disabling <name>` before stop, and the RCON `plugins` listing shows it green (red = disabled = fail).
3. `startup_log_clean`: default matchers (ERROR/FATAL level, exception headers, enable/load errors, datapack load errors) over the log up to the Done line. Spec `logMatchers` replace them (an empty list is refused), `logIgnore` adds ignores. The two built-in ignores cover only noise the sandbox itself causes (no internet: Mojang public-key fetch, Paper version fetch); ignored lines are counted in the evidence.
4. `rcon_checks`: spec commands with `expect`/`expectNot` substrings (colour codes stripped), plus an automatic `datapack list enabled` check per datapack. stop/restart/op/deop/reload are reserved.
5. `clean_stop`: `stop` over RCON (stdin fallback), exit code 0 within `stopSec`, no matcher hits during shutdown.
6. `no_leaks`: our java PID gone, no process anywhere carrying this run's `-Dnxeon.testflight.run=<runId>` marker, no listening port in the reserved range (checked inside the netns and on the host).

**Verdict** (`summary.ts`, pure): required stages come from the spec we sent (boot, log, stop, leaks always; plugins if any plugin; rcon if any command or datapack; plus `requireStages`), not from the runner's flags. Any required fail = `failed`; any required stage missing / `not_run` / "pass" with no evidence = `incomplete`; `busy` and `error` reports are never success. `success` is true only for `passed`.

**Safety on node-2** (shared build host): one flight at a time (`flock -n` on `TF_ROOT/testflight.lock`; a second caller gets `status: "busy"` immediately, exit 75); the server runs in a private network namespace (`unshare --net`, loopback only: no internet, cannot reach or collide with host ports) as uid/gid 65534 with `no_new_privs`, `nice 10`, `-Xmx1g` max, SerialGC, 2 visible CPUs, an RSS watchdog (default 1800 MB) and a hard timeout (runner `totalSec` default 420 + an outer `timeout -s KILL`); kills are only ever by exact PID after re-checking the marker in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`; the run dir and the upload inbox are always removed. Paper jars are fetched from the Fill API only when Fill's sha256 equals the registry pin, then pre-patched once (`paperclip.patchonly`, `bundlerRepoDir`) into a root-owned cache the server cannot write. Plugin jars are re-hashed on node-2 against the hash the invoker computed.

**node-2 layout** (`TF_ROOT=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight`, about 1.5 GB): `jdk/21` (Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, sha256 ce79869e...bcfaee94) and `jdk/25` (Temurin 25.0.4.1+1, sha256 dbb69839...215cf41e), both checked against the Adoptium API; `dl/` (tarballs by sha256); `paper/<sha256>/` (server jar + pre-patched libraries); `runner/` (the invoker pushes `runner.js`/`lib.js` whenever their hash differs from the repo); `runs/` (per-flight dirs, removed); `inbox/` (uploads, removed; `inbox/fx` holds the fixture jars); `reports/<runId>.json`; `classpath/1.21.11.txt` (+ `.sha256`) and `gradle-home/` from resolving the 1.21.11 compile classpath with the template (Gradle 8.14.3 on JDK 21, 24.7 s, 850 MB peak).

**Measured on node-2 (2026-10-10, RAN)**, Done-line wall time from JVM spawn and peak RSS (VmHWM), tiny flat world, `-Xmx1g`:

| Version | JDK | Plugin | Boot (wall) | Paper "Done" | Peak RSS | Whole flight (runner) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | HelloR0 + datapack | 10.6 s | 9.2 s | 803 MB | 13.5 s |
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | TfBroken | 10.6 s | 9.3 s | 762 MB | 12.4 s |
| 26.1.2 b74 | 25 | none | 10.4-10.8 s | 9.3-9.4 s | 722-729 MB | 12.2-16.8 s |
| 1.21.11 b132 | 21 | TfHello + datapack | 18.0 s | 16.6 s | 878 MB | 20.4 s |

One-off per Paper jar: download + pre-patch about 5 s. End to end from the primary over ssh adds about 5-10 s (each ssh connection to node-2 costs about 2.2 s; the invoker uses two: runner hash check, then one call that uploads a tar of artifacts + spec and runs the flight). The research estimate (20-45 s boot, 1.0-1.5 GB) was pessimistic: plan for about 20 s and 1 GB per flight. Capacity: one flight at a time by design, so about 3 flights a minute on 26.x and 2 on 1.21.11, using about 1 GB RAM and up to 2 cores while it runs.

**Results of the real runs (RAN)**: HelloR0 on 26.2 passed all 6 checks (`/hellor0` answered, `function tf:hello` ran, `file/tf_smoke` enabled); TfBroken on 26.2 failed `plugins_enabled` and `startup_log_clean` with the enable-error line, the `IllegalStateException` header and the red `plugins` entry as evidence (boot/stop/leaks still pass); TfHello compiled with JDK 21 `--release 21` against the template-resolved 1.21.11 classpath passed all 6 on Paper 1.21.11; a second flight started 4 s into another came back `busy` with every check `not_run` while the first passed. #!/bin/bash
# Build one Test Flight fixture plugin jar the way the build service does (javac --release N -proc:none against the
# version's resolved classpath file, reproducible `jar --date`). Runs on the build host; fixtures are trusted code.
#   build.sh <fixture-dir> <api-version> <java-home> <release 21|25> <classpath.txt> <out.jar>
set -euo pipefail
SRC="${1:?fixture dir}"; API="${2:?api-version}"; JH="${3:?java home}"; REL="${4:?release}"; CP="${5:?classpath file}"; OUT="${6:?out jar}"
W="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$W/classes"
"$JH/bin/javac" -J-Xmx768m --release "$REL" -proc:none -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$(tr -d '\n' < "$CP")" -d "$W/classes" $(find "$SRC/src" -name '*.java' | sort)
sed "s/@API@/$API/" "$SRC/plugin.yml" > "$W/classes/plugin.yml"
( cd "$W/classes" && find . -type f | sed 's#^\./##' | sort > "$W/entries" )
args=(); while read -r e; do args+=(-C "$W/classes" "$e"); done < "$W/entries"
"$JH/bin/jar" --create --file "$OUT" --date 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z "${args[@]}"
sha256sum "$OUT"

content.thinking:
I'm designing a catalog module that defines the entry type for Minecraft version metadata, plus functions to validate catalog data, load it from JSON, and map a Minecraft version to its family.

I'm also planning a pinning function to pick the right entry while checking Java release compatibility, plus a seeding function to upsert catalog entries into the database by key and family.

Then I'm sketching a pure refs module with a dependent-ID pattern and row type, plus a planEnsure function that decides whether to install, upgrade, add a reference, no-op, or report busy based on the current row state and dependents, and a corresponding planRelease function for removing or decrementing references.

For the service layer, I'm defining a database-like type and working out locking: since the managed-plugin row might not exist yet, I need to upsert a placeholder row first and then lock it with a row-level lock inside a transaction, while handling the possibility of a unique-constraint race from concurrent upserts by retrying.

Now I'm sketching ensureManagedPlugin, which takes injected dependencies (db, installer, catalog) and returns either a success result with action/version/status or a failure with an error code, starting with resolving the pin from the catalog.

In a transaction, I lock the row and compute a plan: busy states return early without changes so the caller can retry, noop/addRef just updates dependents, and install/upgrade updates dependents and marks the row as "installing" before committing. Then outside the transaction I call the installer, and in a follow-up transaction mark success with the installed version, checksum, and install timestamp.

For releaseManagedPlugin, I decrement the ref count, and if that brings it to zero I mark status "removing" with empty dependents, call the installer's remove, then on success set status "removed" with null version and checksum, or on failure set status "failed" with an error and empty dependents -- leaving room for a later ensure or reconcile pass to retry the removal.

I'm also sketching assertUserCanRemove as a guard that checks for remaining dependents before allowing a Mods tab removal, though it's not wired in yet. Then I'm defining the installer interface itself -- a ManagedInstaller with install and remove methods, plus a memoryInstaller test double that tracks installed versions per server and key, records calls, and supports simulating a forced failure on the next operation.

For the real-world implementation gated behind the CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL flag, I'm thinking through what I can safely wire up without overreaching: loading and sha256-verifying the managed artifact, converting it into a Resolution the Mods engine understands (placing it as a plugin-jar keyed by "managed:<key>"), and only then having the real installer act when the flag is enabled.

The problem is the ensure/enqueue flow expects a synchronous result, but the actual install work happens asynchronously in the worker -- so wiring the full path cleanly isn't really possible yet. I'll settle for building and testing the pure artifact-load/verify and Resolution-builder logic, and having the installer refuse with a clear "not wired yet" message (listing what's missing) even when the flag is on, since that's the honest and safe option per the instructions to go only as far as is clearly safe.

Actually, there might be a cleaner path: the engine exports `installOrUpdate(installer, mod, server, deps)`, which takes a FamilyInstaller and EngineDeps. I could build a small FamilyInstaller wrapper whose resolve returns the managed resolution while detect/place delegate to minecraftInstaller, then call this directly from the worker (where GuestFs is available, respecting the per-server lock). I want to check the EngineDeps and installOrUpdate signature to see if this is feasible -- if so, the real installer could be an `engineManagedInstaller(depsFactory)` that runs only inside the worker behind the flag, and I could even test it against LocalGuestFs with the sandbox seed for a strong placement test.

content.thinking:
I'm noting a minor edge case in URL validation between the TS and Java sides, and deciding to cover it with a couple of invalid test configs run through flight tests rather than a shared fixture file. Now I'm moving on to sketching out the main plugin class, starting with the onEnable logic.

For loading packs.json, I'm deciding that a missing file means sending nothing with a log message, while a parse error on first load clears the active config and logs a rejection warning. For reload errors though, I'm debating whether to keep the last good config versus falling back to sending nothing entirely—since there's no persisted "last good" state across restarts, keeping it on reload but clearing it on boot creates an inconsistency, so I'm leaning toward the simpler rule: invalid config always means sending nothing, in both boot and reload cases.

So invalid config at any point (boot, reload, poll) now just empties the active config and records the error, which is fail-safe and consistent, and I'm choosing not to strip packs already applied to online players since that avoids unnecessary churn. For polling, I'll check file mtime and size every 10 seconds using a synchronous Bukkit scheduler task since the file is tiny, and I won't worry about Folia support.

On join, I'm sending each active pack to the player via addResourcePack wrapped in a try/catch per pack, with no artificial delay needed. For reload, packs removed from the new config get explicitly removed from online players, while added or changed packs are deferred to next join—though I'm second-guessing whether changed packs should also push immediately to online players.

Now I'm tracking telemetry through PlayerResourcePackStatusEvent, incrementing per-pack status counters for every outcome (accepted, loaded, declined, various failure types, discarded, downloaded), persisting to a telemetry.json file with pack counts, sent counts, and Bedrock presence info, flushing every 30 seconds and on disable, and loading existing data on startup to continue counting rather than resetting—falling back to a renamed backup file if the existing telemetry is corrupt. For Bedrock support, I'll just detect Geyser/Floodgate plugin presence on enable and log it, skipping per-player Bedrock detection since that would require pulling in the Floodgate API.

I'm planning the /nxpacks command with list, reload, and status subcommands, exposing the Bedrock presence info there and in the telemetry file's platform field. The telemetry file write needs to be atomic—write to a temp file then move with ATOMIC_MOVE—and I'll use Gson for serialization, sticking to plain Bukkit API classes (JavaPlugin, Listener, EventHandler, CommandExecutor, TabCompleter) for broad compatibility.

--
-- Catalog rows are DATA in lib/cyrus/managed/catalog.json; after the tables exist, seed them with
--   npx tsx scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts
-- (idempotent upsert; only the catalog table is written).

input.message:
The pack delivery stack is built and committed on `feature/cyrus-r0`, and all four real Test Flights on node-2 passed. No real Minecraft client was used, so actually sending packs to players, the prompt, kicks for required packs, accept/decline telemetry and pack loading are not verified. Nothing is deployed.

**Built** (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r0`, 7 commits):
- `lib/cyrus/packhost/`: storage interface with a local-disk store and an S3-compatible store. My own SigV4 signer passes AWS's published test vectors. Also: chosen by env, files named `/p/<sha1>.zip`, 100 MB cap, cache headers that never expire, cleanup of old unused packs, the pure pack-config logic, and the config writer. Plus a dev route `app/p/[file]/route.ts` that returns 404 unless the local store is selected.
- `lib/cyrus/managed/`: `catalog.json` (`nxeon-pack-loader` pinned for both 1.21 and 26; no BetterModel) and ref-counted `ensureManagedPlugin` / `releaseManagedPlugin`. The installer is swappable; the real one goes through the Mods engine and only runs with `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` (off).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/packloader/`: the Paper plugin, compiled with `javac --release 21`. One jar works on both versions. The `addResourcePack` signatures are the same in both paper-api jars (1.21.11 and 26.2), checked with javap. It compiles with zero warnings, and two builds gave the same file hash.
- Test Flight can now place config files and rewrite one between commands. Flight specs are in `test/cyrus-packloader-real.ts`.

**Ran:**
- Unit tests: 141/141 pass, including the real Mods engine installing, upgrading and removing the jar on a fake local server. tsc is clean.
- Throwaway DB only: the migration matches the schema with no drift, and the DB tests pass 5/5.
- Real flights: 1.21.11 and 26.2 both passed list, status, reload, the 10-second file watch, and bad config being refused. Two more flights passed: a bad config at boot (server unaffected) and no config file at all. Nothing was left running on node-2.

**Not run:** no real storage bucket was used, the dev route was not tried in a running app, and the real installer was never pointed at a server.

**Migration to approve:** `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-managed-plugins.sql` adds two new tables and changes nothing else. Then run `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts`.

**Owner decisions:**
- Storage provider and bucket (any S3 API; R2 has free egress).
- Public pack domain (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`).
- How long to keep unused packs before cleanup.
- A day for a real-client test.

**Decisions the plan didn't specify:**
- An invalid config sends nothing; it does not keep the previous packs.
- When packs are removed, players lose them right away; new or changed packs arrive on their next join.
- Pack IDs are a UUID derived from the project namespace and pack role, so they stay the same across versions.
- A pack-owner plugin already on the server (Oraxen, Nexo and similar) gives a warning, not a block.
- Pack hosting is off in production by default.

Before the real installer can go live it still needs: a worker job to run it from, the jar on the worker host, a decision on how the Mods tab treats it, and the customer-removal guard hooked into removal paths. The full list is in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` under "Cyrus pack delivery (R0)".
